items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: 'I think it was John Peters that said it, 'Here come J. D.'

ctx.x: said, 'Oh, yeah, he's very nice. I met him, you know, say -- all the children knew he was over on the stage, you see, and that was -- there was kind of happiness with him. They was kind of proud of him, you see. And that part of the city was known as Fourth Ward in Atlanta, Georgia.

And so eventually one day we was talking about him, and he happened to come up the street by himself, Hilliard Street, you see, and (inaudible) and (inaudible), 'Oh, here comes J. D., you know. I think it was John Peters that said it, 'Here come J. D. Said, 'What you going to say to him? Let's talk to -- let's ask him something, you know. Let's ask him about could he teach or help Boodjie with his -- teach Boodjie some tap dancing,' because my cousin was sitting there, first cousin, my Aunt Mary's son, Boby, you…

So sure enough, J. D. turned out to be a lovable person, you know. He had to be lovable, a little boy like that walking his mother, you know, and he was actually like a little man, you see. And he was very nice. So he set down with us. 'What you all -- what you fellows -- what you -- what are you all doing?' you know?
